The older general free-space theorems provide the Schur and linearization ingredients but do not state the exact additive epsilon-isometry family, the sharp power-gauge normalization, or the arbitrary separable non-Schur-source conclusion. Targeted semantic and exact-phrase searches found no statement implying the full claim.

value.rationale: The result changes the scope from one Hilbert source and one square-root gauge to every separable non-Schur Banach source and a continuum of power-snowflake gauges, while retaining one fixed Schur target for all epsilon. The sharp normalization and equality radius quantify exactly how the additive distortion is distributed. This shows that arbitrarily accurate additive metric embeddings can systematically coexist with an absolute exact-isometry obstruction across a broad structural class.
